items.prompt: White's knight can take the black rook or the black pawn, and nothing guards either one. Take the more valuable piece.

claims.statement: Nxe4 wins the rook and nothing is lost back.
No black piece guards the rook.
Taking the pawn is clearly worse than taking the rook.

hints: List what the knight attacks, then compare the counting values.
A rook counts five points; a pawn counts one.
items.explain: Both captures are safe, but the rook counts five points and the pawn one, so the rook is the bigger prize.

feedback_by_move.c3b5: Taking the pawn is safe but wins only one point; the rook stays on the board.

items.prompt: White to move. The queen can take a knight or a pawn. Choose the capture that wins material.

claims.statement: Qxa4 wins a knight and nothing is lost back.
No black piece guards the knight.
One black piece (the e6 pawn) guards the d5 pawn.
Qxd5 is far worse than Qxa4.

hints: Before capturing, ask whether the target is guarded.
One target is guarded by a pawn; a queen is worth far more than a pawn.
Look at the long diagonal from d1.
items.explain: The knight on a4 is unguarded, so Qxa4 wins three points. Qxd5 exd5 trades a queen (nine points) for a pawn (one).

feedback_by_move.d1d5: The d5 pawn is guarded by the e6 pawn, so the queen would be lost for a pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the capture that gains material, even though it will be recaptured.

claims.statement: Nxd7 followed by the king's recapture nets two points.
The rook on d7 is guarded once, by the king.
Nxd7 is the engine's best move.

hints: A capture that will be recaptured can still gain.
Compare the value of the piece taken with the piece that may be lost.
items.explain: Nxd7 Kxd7 gives a knight (three points) for a rook (five), a gain of two even though White's piece is recaptured.

items.prompt: White to move. Which capture wins material?

claims.statement: exd6 wins the knight for at most a pawn.
exd6 is the engine's best move.

hints: The pawn can be recaptured, but compare values.
items.explain: A pawn is the cheapest piece to risk: exd6 wins a knight (three points), and even if the queen retakes, White gives only one point back.
